question: Can conservative current-neighborhood legality filtering avoid the adverse-seed retention effect seen in Y031 while retaining the nine-slot resource bound?
hypothesis: Preference for a cached placement only when it lies in the inner three of a legal five-cell radius-two neighborhood may reduce churn under drift, though it may increase augmenting-path matching cost.
freeze: Fix source, fresh SHA256-keyed cohort and exact inner radius1 preference before first use; do not select after seeing heldout outcomes.
geometry: Exact frozen Y031 geometry: Y030 SHA256-keyed 4-collision templates and 8 episode circular displacements [0,1,6,7,12,13,18,19], seven active motifs of sixteen and circular radius2 matching.
arms: full_neighborhood: when cached cell is currently legal in radius2 neighbor set, prefer it during assignment
inner_preference: when cached cell is currently legal AND in radius1-centered subset of 5 radius2 cells, prefer it; matcher still has radius2 available for all assignments
matching: Same independently verified augmenting path matching, fixed tie ordering, cache writes, occupancy <=9 and evaluator-only returning-key history for both arms. Infer each center uniquely from current 5-cell neighborhood set; no peek at future episodes.
outcomes: Record matching cardinality, per-seed/episode churn, preference reads, calls, writes, per-seed input SHA256 geometry fingerprints. All Hall deficiencies or fingerprint duplicates are explicit scientific outcomes and do not trigger a retry.
primary: INNER_TRUST_TRANSFER if all 4 heldout seed savings full_churn-minus-inner_churn >=0 and total>0; MIXED if signs include both positive and negative; FULL_PREFERENCE_WINS if aggregate savings<0; NO_GAIN otherwise.
validation: Same 9 memory slots and 16 total identities/cells and separate exhaustive Hall oracle; no future history in policy; exact prereg/code/parent SHA, original archive with all outcomes and final full regression.
claim_limit: Synthetic memory placement preference tradeoff; no semantic consolidation or real-world scientific acceptance.
